hypotheses.justification: This instance is not needed to state or to prove the result. Nothing in the statement's binders or conclusion mentions decidable equality on `I`: `VectorPolynomial I ℝ (J j → ℝ)` is `MvPolynomial I ℝ ⊗[ℝ] (J j → ℝ)`, `DegreeLE` is a `Finsupp.weight` condition, `ColumnResiduePattern (Option K) I stride` is `∀ z, ZMod (stride z.2)`, `HasLayerSamplingRank`/`PolynomialRationalApproximation`/`MvPolynomial.homogeneousComponent`/`VectorPolynomial.integerRowPolynomial` need only `[Fintype (J j)]`, and `Finset`, `tsum`, the Bochner integral and `CoefficientTorus`/`affineSampleCoefficientTorus` use only `[Fintype K]`-type data (the internal constructions use `classical`). In the proof the instance is only forwarded to `exists_affine_coefficient_haar_approximation`, whose own `[DecidableEq I]` binder likewise never occurs in its conclusion, so after deleting the binder one starts the proof with `classical` and the instance is synthesized by `Classical.propDecidable` at the call sites; the resulting goal is syntactically the same type.

`_hP` follows from `_hn : (Fintype.card I : ℝ) ≤ P`, because `(Fintype.card I : ℝ) ≥ 0`. So in the proof the binder can be replaced by `have hP : 0 ≤ P := by have := Nat.cast_nonneg (Fintype.card I); linarith`, and the rest of the proof (which only uses `hP` when calling `exists_affine_coefficient_haar_approximation`) is unchanged. `_hP` is not otherwise mentioned in the statement (P itself is a separate binder). Note that `_hP` and `_hn` can even be deleted simultaneously, since both follow from `_hd` (see the next entry).

`_hn` follows from `_hd : (Fintype.card (Option K × I) : ℝ) ≤ P`, since `Fintype.card (Option K × I) = (Fintype.card K + 1) * Fintype.card I ≥ Fintype.card I` (`Fintype.card_prod`, `Fintype.card_option`), hence after casting to ℝ `(Fintype.card I : ℝ) ≤ (Fintype.card (Option K × I) : ℝ) ≤ P` (using `(Fintype.card K : ℝ) + 1 ≥ 1` and `(Fintype.card I : ℝ) ≥ 0`). So one can prove `have hn : (Fintype.card I : ℝ) ≤ P := ...` and keep the rest of the proof; `_hn` does not occur anywhere else in the statement.

`_hη` is implied by `_happrox`. Indeed `CoefficientTorus (K := K) U` is inhabited (`CoefficientArray U = ∀ s : CoefficientSlot K m, U s.1` is a Pi of submodules, hence nonempty, and the torus is its quotient), so taking `b := false` and any point `x` of the torus, `_happrox false x` gives `‖(D x : ℂ) - coefficientTorusFourierSum U (frequency false) (c false) x‖ ≤ η`, and the left side is a norm, hence `≥ 0`; therefore `0 ≤ η`. After deleting `_hη` one proves `have hη : 0 ≤ η := (norm_nonneg _).trans (happrox false ⟨some element⟩)` and runs the original proof (which only needs `hη` to pass it on to `exists_affine_coefficient_haar_approximation`); the degenerate case `η < 0` is vacuous because then `_happrox` cannot hold.
